title: Local dimension as the maximum of component dimensions on a locally algebraic scheme
statement: Let $k$ be a field [def-weil-field], let $X$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], and let $f:X\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ be locally of finite type [def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. For every point $x\in X$, the local topological dimension [def-kun-topological-dimension-at-point] is the maximum of the topological Krull dimensions [def-kun-topological-krull-dimension] of the irreducible components [def-weil-irreducible-components] containing $x$: $$\dim_x X=\max\{\dim C:C\text{ is an irreducible component of }X,\ x\in C\}.$$ Each $C$ has its subspace topology [def-kun-subspace-topology]; the displayed family is nonempty and its maximum is attained. No irreducibility, equidimensionality, separatedness or quasi-compactness of $X$ is assumed. For empty $X$ there is no point $x$, so the assertion is vacuous.

proof.text: For an inducing map g:A→B and a∈A, dim_a A≤dim_g(a) B: pull back each open neighbourhood V of g(a), then use subspace dimension monotonicity on its inducing restriction and take infima. In particular homeomorphisms preserve local dimension, by applying this inequality in both directions.

Let C be a component through x. Give C its reduced induced closed scheme structure j:Y→X, with Y homeomorphic to C. The scheme Y is irreducible and its composite to Spec k is locally of finite type. Lift x to y∈Y. The irreducible locally algebraic dimension theorem gives dim C=dim Y=dim_y Y. The inducing inequality from step 1 gives dim_y Y≤dim_x X. This proves the bound for every component.

Choose an affine open neighbourhood U of x. Its ring R=Γ(U, O_X) is finite type over k by the definition of locally finite type. The affine homeomorphism U≅Spec R and open-subspace invariance identify dim_x X with dim_p Spec R at the corresponding prime p. The affine component theorem supplies a component D through p whose dimension is this value.

Map D into X along the open embedding Spec R≅U→X. Its image is irreducible, so it is contained in a maximal irreducible subset C of X, by the general existence theorem for components. This C contains x. The induced embedding D→C gives dim_x X=dim D≤dim C, while step 2 gives the reverse inequality. Hence C attains the required maximum. Empty X has no x.
